title: Wall time per task is recorded by stage and printed
description: Users reported that development through the plugin is slow, and a paired measurement put the plugin near three times a plain session's wall time per task while the writer alone was faster than plain. The plugin cannot say where the rest goes: a gate run records its duration, and nothing else does. A writer or reviewer session's own duration is dropped when its cost is read, the time spent selecting affected suites runs before the gate's clock starts, a dispatch for a writer or a reviewer carries no time at all, and the drive's launch stamps die with its state file when the phase ends. This phase records each stage where the plan keeps it (the task in its shard), because the evidence ledger and the drive state are due to be removed and the plan and git are what remains. Nothing here makes a task faster; it makes the next phase's choices measurable. Exit: on a task driven end to end in a fixture, the stage figures and the unattributed remainder add up to the task's whole window, and a stage with no source says so instead of printing zero.
desiredOutcome: Every task the drive runs leaves in its shard how long each stage took: each writer round, each recorded gate run with the time spent choosing what to run, a base measurement, the review, the record commit, and the time a handed-out step waited before it started. /audit:status prints the figures and their JSON form carries them, each with the record it was read from, so wall time per task can be measured beside cost and quality.

tasks.title: A writer or reviewer session's record carries how long the session took, read from the session's own result
tasks.description: The session runner (run-agent-session.py) reads the last result event of the session's stream for the cost and drops what the same event says about time. Its record gains the result's duration_ms, duration_api_ms and num_turns, and the session's start time (the stamp the stream file's name already carries), under the names durationMs, durationApiMs, numTurns and startedAt. A figure the result does not carry, or carries as something that is not a number, is left out and the record's line names the absence; it is never written as zero. Dependants you answer for: drive-phase.py reads this record for the session's cost and exit (note_sessions, session_note, the dispatch read-back) and must keep parsing it unchanged; the line run-agent-session.py prints is parsed by the drive and by the measurement harness outside this repository, so its existing fields keep their order and spelling and new ones are appended; every fixture in tests/test_drive_phase.py that writes a session record by hand must still load. Acceptance: (1) a record written from a stream whose result carries duration_ms, duration_api_ms and num_turns holds the three figures and the start time; (2) a stream with no result event writes a record with none of the three and a line that says no result was read; (3) a result whose duration_ms is a string or a negative number is recorded as absent, with the reason, and not as zero; (4) a record written before this change, with none of the new keys, is read by the drive exactly as before.

tasks.title: A task has one timing record in its shard: stages with a start, a length and the record each was read from, and a first start that survives a restart
tasks.description: Add the optional task key timing: an object with firstStartedAt and stages, where a stage is kind, startedAt, ms, basis and optional round and runId. The kinds are a closed list: writer, gate, selection, base, reviewer, commit, wait. One new helper module, plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/_task_timing.py, holds the pure functions every writer and reader uses: build a stage, append it to a task, and summarize a task into per-kind totals, the whole window from firstStartedAt to completedAt, and the unattributed remainder, each with its basis and with an absent source named rather than read as zero. task.startedAt is re-stamped on every restart today, so the first start is lost; starting a task now sets timing.firstStartedAt once and never moves it. The key is additive: a plan that never writes it validates and behaves exactly as before, and COMPATIBILITY.md says so beside its other additive keys. A new module owes the five things CLAUDE.md lists for a file under scripts/ (suite, layer in tools/lints/_deps.py, tree line and section in PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, the path preamble; it is a helper, so no entry guard). Dependants you answer for: the schema and the validator's vocabulary must agree (_manifest_vocab.py KNOWN_TASK and SCHEMA_ANCHORS, _help.schema_vocab_drift, the unknown-key warning in _manifest_phases.py); every committed example plan and rendered artifact must still validate and render byte for byte, since none carries the key; audit-task.py's start, reopen, move and cancel verbs copy or reset task fields and must carry timing the way they carry notes; the panel's writer rewrites tasks and must not drop a key it does not know. Acceptance: (1) a task carrying a well-formed timing validates with no warning, and a task without it validates exactly as today; (2) a stage with an unknown kind, a negative ms or no basis is a validator finding that names the task and the stage; (3) a restart keeps firstStartedAt while startedAt moves; (4) the summary of a task whose stages cover part of its window reports the remainder as unattributed, and the parts add up to the window; (5) the summary of a task with no completedAt, or no timing, says which is missing and gives no total; (6) move and reopen keep the record.

tasks.title: A recorded gate run says how long choosing what to run took, beside how long the steps took
tasks.description: run-test-gate.py starts its clock at the first step, so the time it spends gathering the affected suites and reading the gate's reach is in no figure at all. The recorded row gains selectionMs: the time from the start of that work to the first step, measured on the same monotonic clock. durationMs keeps its meaning, the steps alone, because other code decides on it. A run that selected nothing (a reused verdict, a gate with no derived part) records selectionMs for the work it did do, and a row written before this change carries no such key, which reads as not recorded. Dependants you answer for: _evidence_io.gate_mean_ms decides whether a gate runs in the foreground from durationMs and must give the same answer on the same rows; the doctor grades meta.gateBudgetMs from durationMs; audit-usage compares narrowed and phase gates and reused and measured runs from durationMs; the report and the panel list a row's steps and its took figure and must render a row with the new key unchanged; the row's hash chain covers the row as written, so a new key must enter the row before it is hashed; COMPATIBILITY.md lists the evidence row's additive keys and gains this one. Acceptance: (1) a recorded task gate with a derived part carries selectionMs and its durationMs equals the sum the steps took, as before; (2) gate_mean_ms over a ledger holding old and new rows returns what it returned over the same rows without the key; (3) a row without selectionMs is read as not recorded by every reader, never as zero; (4) the ledger's verifier accepts a chain holding both kinds of row.

tasks.title: The drive writes a task's stages as it reads each step back, and stamps a writer or reviewer dispatch when it hands it out
tasks.description: When the drive reads a finished step back it appends one stage to the task's timing through the shared helper: a writer round from the session record (start, length, round), a recorded gate run from its ledger row (runId, start, length) with its selection time as a stage of its own, a base measurement from its row, the reviewer session from its record, and the record commit timed around the commit verb. A dispatch for a writer or a reviewer is stamped when it is handed out, the way a gate's is, and the gap between a hand-out and the step's own start is a wait stage, so time the orchestrator spent not calling next is counted rather than lost. The stages go into the shard in a write the drive already makes for that step (the session note, the verdict pointer, the close): this change adds no commit and no locked write of its own, because a metric that slows the thing it measures is wrong by construction. A source that is missing (a session record with no duration, a row that could not be read) appends nothing for that stage and the summary then reports the time as unattributed. A wave member writes its stages in its own tree's shard and integration carries them. Dependants you answer for: the drive's state file and its one-use launch marks (gateLaunched, baseMeasured, phaseGateLaunched) keep their meaning; the wait and dispatch step texts the orchestrator and the prompt hook read keep their wording apart from a since clause where one is added; commit-task-work's refusal on an unexpected shard change must not fire on a timing append; verify-invariants' commit-scope check reads what a task commit staged; tests/test_drive_phase.py holds fixtures of every step and its decision table. Do not edit plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md (it sits at its context ceiling); put any text the orchestrator needs into the step the drive prints. Acceptance: (1) a fixture task driven from start to done through a writer round, a green gate, a review and the commit leaves writer, selection, gate, reviewer and commit stages whose figures match their sources, and the summary's parts add up to the window; (2) a red gate followed by a base measurement and a second writer round leaves two writer stages with their rounds, two gate stages and a base stage; (3) a hand-out read back after a delay leaves a wait stage of that length; (4) a session record with no duration leaves no writer stage and the summary reports that time as unattributed; (5) the number of commits and of locked manifest writes the drive makes for the fixture task is the same as before the change; (6) a wave member's stages reach the phase tree's shard at integration.

tasks.title: A session's recorded duration covers every stretch of the session, an oversized figure cannot crash the runner, and a repeated gate's selection time holds none of its duration
tasks.description: Findings of the phase review, fixed before sign-off. (a) run-agent-session.py reads the time figures of the LAST result event alone. A headless session woken by a background task writes one init and one result per stretch, and duration_ms and num_turns are per stretch (tools/stream-cost.py states this and sums them; only the cost is a whole-session figure on the last result). So a ten-minute session whose last stretch took five seconds is recorded as five seconds, with nothing saying one stretch was read. Record the whole session: sum the per-stretch figures the way tools/stream-cost.py pairs init and result events, and when the stretches cannot be paired, leave the figure out and name it in timingAbsent with that reason. A shipped script cannot import a repository tool, so the pairing rule is written in the runner and both copies are pinned to one fixture stream by a case; say so in the docstring. (b) A JSON integer too large for a float makes the finiteness test raise, and nothing catches it: the runner dies after the session ran and was paid for, with no printed line and no record. Such a figure is not a usable number: record it as absent with the reason, and make the timing reading unable to take the runner down whatever the stream holds, with the failure named in timingAbsent rather than swallowed. (c) On a repeated gate run, durationMs is measured from the identity lookup and selectionMs from the earlier start of gathering, both to the same end, so the repeat's duration lies inside its selection and a reader adding the two counts it twice; the key's own comment says beside, never inside. Make the two disjoint on every path. (d) On a measured run the selection figure also holds the reading of the tree taken before the first step; say so where the key is defined instead of listing only the gathering, the lookup and the reach reading. (e) The start stamp is when the runner named the stream file, before it prepares and launches the session; the docstrings that call it the session's start say what it is. (f) The case that holds gate_mean_ms unchanged by the key cannot fail against the defect it is named for, and the case that only checks the key's spelling asserts nothing: replace each with a case that fails when selection time is folded into a step's duration, or remove it and say which case carries the claim. Dependants you answer for: the drive's read_sessions, session_note and session_stages, which read durationMs and startedAt from the record; the printed result line, unchanged; the ledger row's hash, taken after the key is set; tests/test_stream_cost.py if a shared fixture stream is added there. Acceptance: (1) a stream of two paired stretches records the sums of duration and turns; (2) stretches that cannot be paired leave the figures out with the reason; (3) an integer too large for a float is absent with the reason, and the runner prints its line and writes its record; (4) a repeated run's selectionMs plus durationMs equals the time from the start of gathering to the end, with no overlap; (5) every docstring this task touches states what the code does; (6) no case added or kept by this task passes with its feature removed.

tasks.title: The phase's time line counts finished tasks only, a record that cannot be read is named instead of shown as unattributed time, and long windows print in hours
tasks.description: Findings of the phase review, fixed before sign-off. (a) The phase's time line says it is taken over finished tasks, and takes every task that has a window. Cancelling a task stamps its completedAt, so a cancelled task that was once started enters the median, the totals and the count: a phase with one task done and one cancelled reads as two finished tasks, beside a progress bar that says one. Take the line over tasks whose status is done; name the tasks left out and why (cancelled, not finished, no window) in the JSON aggregate, and say cancelled tasks are left out where the line is documented. (b) summarize reads a stages value that is not a list as no stages, so the whole window is returned and printed as unattributed time with nothing named missing, against the module's own rule that an unreadable source is named. Name it under missing and give no attributed or unattributed figure; the same for a stage that fails stage_problems, which today is summed or skipped without a word. Status then prints the cell as not readable rather than as a measured window. (c) The documents say the gate reads none of the record. A malformed record is a validator finding, and invalid is a default gate condition, so it can turn the gate red. Say what is true: the gate reads no timing figure, only the validator's verdict on the record. (d) The time cell has a third value, no window, that no document lists and no case renders; neither does any case render the overrun clause. Document the value and what produces it (a record whose first start is absent, or a completion before the first start) and add a case for each. (e) A reopened task's window runs from its first start to its new completion, so the time it sat closed is unattributed and enters the median. That follows the rule that the first start never moves; state it where the window is documented, since the median is read as time worked. tasks.title: The commit stage times the commit alone, a close that changes nothing keeps its stages, and a stage the drive could not read is said so
tasks.description: Findings of the phase review, fixed before sign-off. (a) The commit stage is timed around everything the drive's commit step does. When the commit verb refuses a path the writer touched outside the task's files and the drive sets it aside, that step runs a red-first proof and a whole gate before the second commit, and that gate is also written as a gate stage of its own. So the gate's length is counted twice, the task's stages overrun its window, and a figure of half a minute or more is presented as a measured commit under a basis that says the commit verb was timed. Time the commit verb's own calls, sum them when there are two, and let the proof and the gate between them be the stages they already are. (b) The close the no-change answer makes passes no stages and never marks them carried, so on the route where every queued stage rides the close a task closed that way loses all of them, silently. Every close the drive makes carries the queue through one function. (c) A stage whose source cannot be read (the ledger or a row unreadable, a row with no start or length, an agent hand-out with no stamp) appends nothing, which is right, and says nothing, which is not: failures to write are already visible and failures to read are not. Add a line to what the step did, naming the stage and the reason, once per source. (d) The end of an agent's stage falls back to the returned file's modification time under a basis that says no journal row files that return. For an executor that is false when the row exists and could not be read; say which happened. For a reviewer the modification time is the only source, and it moves when the file is rewritten by a stash, a branch switch or a copy: say in the basis that it is a modification time and can move later, never earlier, rather than presenting it as the moment of filing. (e) Cases with no check: nothing asserts that the journal row of a note or a close carrying a stage names the timing change, so removing that change leaves every case green; the commit stage is asserted only to be zero or more, which is why (a) was invisible; a refused note keeping its stages for the close, and a close refused and retried appending each stage once, are stated in comments and held by no case. Add each. Dependants you answer for: the decision table and step texts in tests/test_drive_phase.py; the one-use launch marks and the state file's shape across resume and drop_state; the rule that timing never blocks a gate, a commit or a close; the count of commits and locked writes per task, unchanged; the stage shapes status and the summary read. Do not edit plugins/audit/reference/orchestrator.md. Acceptance: (1) on the set-aside path the commit stage equals the commit verb's own time within the case's clock, the second gate is one gate stage, and the summary shows no overrun; (2) a task closed by the no-change answer has its queued stages in the shard; (3) an unreadable ledger at read-back leaves no gate stage and one line naming it and the reason; (4) each fallback basis says what was read and why; (5) the journal row of a note and of a close that carried a stage names the change, and removing it turns a case red; (6) a refused note's stages reach the shard at the close, once; (7) no case added or kept by this task passes with its feature removed.
